html:
The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms is the bill of rights in Canada's constitution. It came into force on 17 April 1982, as part of the Constitution Act, 1982.

Until then, Canada's constitution was a British law, and changing it needed a vote in London. Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau set out to "patriate" it: bring it home, with a way to amend it in Canada and a charter of rights added. After long talks, nine of the ten provinces agreed. Quebec did not, and still has not signed. Queen Elizabeth II proclaimed the new constitution in Ottawa.

  • It protects freedom of religion, speech and assembly, voting rights, legal rights and equality.
  • It guarantees rights to English and French language schooling.
  • Section 1 allows "reasonable limits" on rights.
  • The "notwithstanding clause" lets parliaments override some rights for five years at a time.

The Charter gave Canadian courts, led by the Supreme Court of Canada, power to strike down laws. Rulings under it struck down the abortion law in 1988 and opened the way to same sex marriage in the 2000s.
sum: The Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms is the bill of rights in Canada's constitution. It came into force on 17 April 1982, as part of the Constitution Act, 1982.
